The words

Let God the Father live
For ever on our tongues;
Sinners from his first love derive
The ground of all their songs.

Ye saints, employ your breath
In honour to the Son,
Who bought your souls from hell and death
By offering up his own.

Give to the Spirit praise
Of an immortal strain,
Whose light and power and grace conveys
Salvation down to men.

While God the Comforter
Reveals our pardon'd sin,
O may the blood and water bear
The same record within.

To the great One and Three
That seal this grace in heaven,
The Father, Son, and Spirit, be
Eternal glory given.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum Ab and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on l, (F), on the word “Let”, as a pickup before the first full bar.
  • Count the time. 4/4 means four crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l t. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book III, prepared for the Lord's Supper, hymn 28, headed “1st. S. M”.

Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.

  • Words (1707): Isaac Watts (1674–1748)
  • Melody (1579): From William Daman's Psalter, 1579

Questions about Let God the Father Live

What is the doh of Let God the Father Live?

In this version, in F minor, doh is Ab. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Let God the Father Live start on?

It starts on l, (F in F minor), a pickup on the word “Let” before the first full bar. Find doh first, then sing up or down to l,.

Is Let God the Father Live in the public domain?

Yes. Isaac Watts died in 1748; the words were first published in 1707 and the music in 1579. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
